newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.S. plans to tighten Helms-Burton law - Euro-MP.
newsitem.headline: U.S. plans to tighten Helms-Burton law - Euro-MP.

text.p: The U.S. Congress is planning to step up measures against foreign firms trading with Cuba, in spite of an EU-U.S. agreement to end a trans- Atlantic row over U.S. anti-Cuba laws, a leading Euro-MP said on Thursday.

The foreign affairs committee in Congress proposed on May 6 an amendment to the so-called Helms-Burton Act which would oblige the U.S. secretary of state to compile a regular blacklist of companies and individuals deemed to have violated the Act, Luciana Castellina, head of the European Parliament's external economic relations committee, told Euro-MPs.
The proposal, seen by Reuters, came less than three weeks after the EU formally agreed to suspend a World Trade Organisation (WTO) challenge to the Act.
In return, the White House agreed to seek to change a key provision of the Act which bars executives of companies that invest in disputed properties in Cuba from entering the U.S.

The Congress committee's draft amendment, which would have to be approved by the full Congress, obliges the secretary of state to submit to the Congress and the U.S. Senate every three months a blacklist of those being investigated for "trafficking" in U.S. property expropriated by the Cuban government.
The Helms-Burton Act, an amalgam of U.S. anti-Cuba laws, has outraged Washington's trading partners because it threatens non-U.S. businesses with interests in Cuba.
Castellina told the parliament the Congress committee's move raised doubts about U.S. willingness to abide by the trans- Atlantic accord.

Replying to Euro-MP concerns that the EU had given in to the Americans too easily, EU Commissioner Hans van den Broek said the EU had repeatedly warned it would revive the WTO disputes panel if Washington reneged on the deal.
Despite van den Broek's assurances, the parliament adopted a resolution urging the EU's executive Commission to renew its WTO challenge.
